reason: The hypothesis relies on specific claims about passive film behavior, film removal by wear, and repassivation kinetics in high-entropy alloys, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge covers general tribo-corrosion concepts, but the application to HEAs and the specific mechanistic cycle require supporting data that are absent.
premises: HEAs form a protective passive oxide film that provides corrosion resistance under static conditions
Mechanical sliding locally removes this passive film, exposing bare metal
Exposed metal corrodes rapidly until the film repassivates
The balance between mechanical film removal rate and electrochemical repassivation rate governs overall degradation
A more robust or faster-forming passive film reduces coupled tribo-corrosion degradation
